title: Safe sleep — AAP basics for newborns
summary: Simple sleep environment choices reduce risk. Same room, separate surface.
whatsNormal:
Newborns sleep a lot — often 14–17 hours in a 24-hour period, in short stretches.

• Back to sleep for every sleep (naps and night)
• Firm, flat sleep surface with a fitted sheet only — no pillows, blankets, or bumpers
• Room-sharing (same room) without bed-sharing is recommended for at least the first 6 months
• Pacifier at sleep time is OK once breastfeeding is established, if you use one

Swaddling is fine if hips can move and you stop when baby shows signs of rolling.
watchFor: Falling asleep with baby on a couch, armchair, or adult bed — high risk
Overheating: sweaty neck, flushed skin, or room too warm
Products marketed as "sleep positioners" or inclined sleepers — not recommended
Tired parents nodding off while holding baby on a soft surface
callDoctorIf: Episodes of breathing pause, color change, or choking during sleep — describe to your pediatrician promptly
Baby turns blue or gray around lips during feeds or sleep — seek emergency care
You need help with safe sleep when exhausted — ask your clinician or postpartum support; plan shifts if possible
